newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to extend one trillion won to banks.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to extend one trillion won to banks.

text.p: South Korea's finance and economy ministry said on Thursday it would extend one trillion won in soft loans to 33 domestic banks from April 28 to May 17.

The loans will carry an annual interest rate of 10 percent, which is 2.5-3.0 percentage points lower than average lending rates in South Korea. A ministry official said the loans would help relieve a short-term liquidity shortage following value-added-tax payments during the period.
This is the first time the ministry has directly extended loans to domestic banks, as the central Bank of Korea has been the lender to those banks.

The official said the ministry would extend 500 billion won in proportion to banks' loans to small and medium-sized companies. The rest will be allocated in accordance to the size of banks' purchases of state bonds with maturities of three to 10 years.
"We plan to release further soft loans to banks at the end of July, October and next January when tax payments are due," he added.
